art.caption: The push bar is not where the push bar is.

lines.text: You reach back for the push bar instinctively.
Painted breeze block, cold, and a seam of mortar where your thumb expects a steel push bar.
Hmmph.
You go along the wall with the flat of your hand. Two metres to the left, and back to the right.
Oh Christ oh fuck oh God I came in eleven seconds ago and I have already lost my exit, great great great great grea-
Don't panic.
Alright, let's take a breath.
I'll find it on the way out, when I'm not standing here like this. When I'm not in the middle of a room with my flashlight off.
Which is true. It is also exactly the reasoning that keeps a man *inside* a building and not darting back home to the kind of cotidian safety only jaffa cakes and Mr. Whiskers can provide.
But for now, you trudge along in the dark.
Speaking of, let's find that flashlight. It should be in my bag, I just had it a second ago.
Say it out loud. It works. It has always worked, and there is nobody here to hear it.

choices.text: "I want to hear that natatorium. Six metres of tile and no water."
"Four hundred quid. I am not walking out on a paid job."
"You don't leave a building angry. You finish, and you thank it."

choices.text: "Nobody's expecting me till Thursday. That's fine. That has always been fine."
"Sarah'll have gone up. She won't check the drive till morning."
